en.title: Warren Buffett Told His Trustee to Put 90% of His Wife’s Inheritance in One S&P 500 Fund and Named Vanguard. On $500,000, VOO Costs $150 a Year and SPY Costs $472.50
en.desc: Buffett's will tells a trustee exactly where 90% of his widow's inheritance should go, and he names the fund company but not the ticker. Two S&P 500 ETFs fit his instructions, yet one quietly costs more every year.

en.title: The Dow Jones Just Had Its Best Week Since October 2022
en.desc: One week after the Dow's worst stretch since 2020, a violent rebound has investors cheering. Thin holiday volume, a lingering November loss, and one last trading day on Monday could decide whether the bounce is real or a mirage.

en.title: A $500,000 Stake in VOO Lost $41,700 in the S&P 500’s Worst Week Since April 2025. Since 1950, Buying After a 10% Drop Has Returned 15% on Average a Year Later
en.desc: One brutal week erased tens of thousands from a retiree-sized VOO position, then Monday's rally changed the math. Decades of market history suggest what comes after drops like this, but today's slide may not qualify yet.

en.title: SWAN Was Built to Survive a Crash. It Cost Holders $180,330 Against VOO on $300,000 in Five Years
en.desc: SWAN aims to cushion a market crash with Treasuries and a small slice of options. The same design that soothes nervous investors carries a steep price in rising markets, and retirees should know exactly what they pay for that comfort.

en.title: BofA Sees S&P 500 Rising 8% in 2027: Are Your ETFs Ready for a Soft Landing?
en.desc: BofA forecasts 8.3% S&P 500 upside by 2027, but fading buybacks and rising risks make these three low-cost ETFs worth a closer look.

en.title: The 3 ETFs to Add at 52 When Your Only Investment Is the Company Stock You Buy Every Paycheck
en.desc: Your paycheck and your nest egg ride on the same company, so one bad quarter could hit you twice just as retirement nears. Three Vanguard funds offer a way out, but the tax rules on your ESPP shares can trip you up first.

en.title: $2,000,000 In QQQ At The 2000 Peak Ran Out
en.desc: If you plan to retire soon and most of your savings sit in tech funds, this autumn has been hard to watch. Invesco QQQ, the fund that tracks the Nasdaq 100 index, closed at $633.93 on Wednesday, Nov 25. That is 16.6% below its record close on Oct 6.

en.title: One Vanguard ETF Hunts for Stocks That Are Cheap, Rising, and Financially Strong All at Once. Almost Nobody Owns It
en.desc: Your index fund buys everything, good or bad. This Vanguard fund screens for multiple traits at once and has quietly left the S&P 500 behind this year, yet it holds a sliver of the assets. What's the catch for retirees?

en.title: What's Left Of $1 Million In VOO And BND?
en.desc: Retirement turns a portfolio into a paycheck. Every statement starts to feel like a report card on the choices you made. The quiet question is always the same. Am I doing all right.

en.title: $1 Million In BND Five Years Ago: Barely Back
en.desc: Bonds are meant to be the calm half of a stock-and-bond mix. This article looks at what the last five years were like for someone who already owned bonds.

en.title: Is XRP a Good Investment for Building Wealth by 2035?
en.desc: One bank sees XRP soaring more than 14 times higher, yet five-year holders have little to show for their patience. Supply keeps swelling, Ripple controls the spigot, and a steadier rival waits. Which path actually builds wealth?
